_about: What the Issuer Security & Deployment Health section looks for. Each file is compared with the repository by SHA-256 like every other file; when it differs, the 'needs' texts say whether it still has the security changes (modified) or not (outdated). tools/site-doctor-build.js checks that every text below occurs in the repository's copy of the file and that the owner-proof classes match lib/owner-proof.php, so a refactor cannot leave a stale check behind.

files.role: Limits and polices this issuer's requests to other domains
files.matters: An older copy shares one outbound budget between all visitors, so one caller can use up the key lookups or one peer's revocation checks and make legitimate cross-domain claims fail.

needs.label: separate verify, drop and relay budgets

files.role: The issuer's shared library: names the budget class of each outbound lookup and holds the drop-expiry rules
files.matters: Without the class names every lookup is counted as 'relay', so credential checks are not protected by their own reserved budget. Without the drop-expiry rules a relayed claim is accepted for an owner authorisation of any age.

needs.label: revocation list lookups counted as verify
suspension list lookups counted as verify

files.role: Claims a world drop, relaying to the issuing domain when the item is foreign
files.matters: An older copy counts drop relays with trade and mail relays, and does not tell the issuing domain when the drop was accepted.

needs.label: acceptance time sent with the claim

files.role: Places a credential in a world as a drop
files.matters: An older copy accepts an owner's drop authorisation of any age.

files.role: Receives a claim relayed from another domain for an item this issuer issued
files.matters: Its own code was not changed by the recent hardening; a difference matters only if the file is an old copy that predates the owner-intent checks.
